sanskrit_verse: अन्याक्षरनिवेशेन अन्यार्थगमनेन च । आकुलं च क्रियादानं क्रिया चैवाकुला भवेत् ॥
transliteration: anyākṣaraniveśena anyārthagamanena ca | ākulaṃ ca kriyādānaṃ kriyā caivākulā bhavet ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When action is performed through misrepresentation of symbols or intent, leading to confusion in execution and outcome, both the initiation and performance of such action become disturbed and devoid of dharmic clarity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in conscious intention aligned with Dharma
Causation arises from clarity of symbolic and semantic alignment
Capacity-based responsibility requires integrity of expression and reception
Restoration logic demands realignment of action with original dharmic purpose
Consciousness alignment ensures that all acts reflect truthful cognition
executable_legal_axioms: IF an act involves deliberate substitution of signs OR distortion of meaning THEN the actor bears full capacity-responsibility for resulting dissonance
IF communication leads to actionable misunderstanding due to symbolic misalignment THEN restoration includes re-cognition and re-expression by the originator
IF a transaction lacks semantic integrity at point of initiation THEN it shall not be recognized as valid within dharma-adjudicated systems
ALL actions must maintain causal continuity between declared intent, symbolic form, and realized effect ELSE they are subject to completion protocols
supreme_court_application: In adjudication, when disputes arise from contractual or communicative ambiguity caused by intentional or negligent symbol manipulation, the threshold of responsibility lies with the initiating party who failed to ensure semantic clarity. The court must restore integrity through compelled re-alignment rather than punitive damages.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that distorted signs produce distorted outcomes. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals the sequential degradation of meaning from source to effect. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of conscious involvement in the distortion. Non-punitive reality rule affirms correction, not condemnation, as the path to resolution.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiator must publicly re-express original intent using unambiguous symbols
Affected parties undergo guided recognition process to dissolve residual confusion
All involved engage in completion ritual reaffirming correct symbolic usage
Systemic safeguards installed to prevent recurrence through automated semantic validation
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Action derives its validity from conscious clarity, not mechanical execution. Misaligned signs breed chaos; restored awareness restores order. Dharma prevails through cognition corrected, not souls condemned. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
